subject: [P0] StratusCare production latency spike — eastus AZ1 — routing/failover request
messages:
From: Lena Park <lena.park@stratuscare.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike - eastus AZ1 - urgent

Hi Mateo,

We just started seeing a major latency surge and increased 502/504 errors from our production fleet hitting eastus AZ1 (many sessions are spiking from ~100ms to >1.5s and throughput is dropping by ~40%). Our internal ops dashboard shows request queues backing up and a material drop in completed inference requests. This is impacting our billing page and chat flows — multiple customers are complaining.

Attached are a short CSV of recent request latencies and a screenshot of our monitoring (perf-spike-graphs.png). Can Redwood switch routing away from eastus AZ1 to eastus2 (or a nearby healthy AZ) while you investigate? We need a temporary routing/failover that preserves session affinity as much as possible; long-running chats are sensitive.

We’re available for a quick bridge. Please advise ETA.

--
Lena Park
SRE Lead, StratusCare
ops@stratuscare.com

In parallel:
- Recommend immediate traffic redistribution from eastus AZ1 -> eastus2 (priority route) for StratusCare only. This is a routing policy update we can push within ~12-18 minutes.
- Ops: confirm if we can reserve 2x burst nodes in eastus2 to avoid cold-start amplification during cutover. Cost estimate ~$$ (TBD).

Hannah

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike - eastus AZ1 - urgent

On Tue, Oct 2, 2028 at 8:28 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ack — we’re activating the regional degradation runbook (East US).

Short technical summary:
- Root cause candidate: a small subset of GPU workers in eastus AZ1 hit an input-length distribution spike (long conversational histories) which triggered suboptimal kernel path and excessive KV-cache thrash for that model variant. That caused CPU/GPU contention, request queueing and a downstream 5xx cascade.
- Remediation plan (immediate):
  1) Geo-redispatch StratusCare traffic from eastus AZ1 -> eastus2 (no model downgrade) and keep session-affinity via sticky session cookie mapping; this avoids KV warm penalty for the majority of sessions.
  2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV-cache seeding for StratusCare in eastus2 (preload recent KV keys from snapshot) — takes ~8-12 minutes depending on snapshot size.
  3) If cache warming isn't sufficient, fall back to temporary model variant with lighter KV usage for chats >1k tokens.

I’ll start the routing change now (pushing policy), and Ops will queue a cache preload job. ETA to measurable impact: 20–30 minutes. I attached perf graphs showing the KV miss curve and CPU utilization (perf-spike-graphs.png).

Soojin
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: VP Sales <vp.sales@redwood.com>, VP Ops <vp.ops@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: StratusCare P0 - request for priority capacity + credit approval

Team — moving to exec: this is an active P0 affecting a top-20 customer. Summary: eastus AZ1 is degrading and we are pushing a geo-redispatch to eastus2 for StratusCare only; Soojin estimates measurable improvement in 20–30 minutes after cache seeding.

Requests for immediate approval:
1) Authorize allocating 2x reserved burst nodes in eastus2 for up to 6 hours (to be billed to Redwood) so we avoid additional cold-start flakiness during cutover. Estimated spend: ~$1,800 for the window.
2) Approve a customer remedial credit of 20% for the impacted 6-hour window (we can offer a draft credit PDF; attached: stratuscare-credit-offer-draft.pdf).
3) Sign-off to join a 30-minute exec bridge with StratusCare at epoch+15 to confirm remediation and next steps.

This ask is time sensitive. Please reply with approval or counter.

Thanks, Marissa

Redwood Inference
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>

Lena / StratusCare ops — quick update and plan: 

1) We have pushed a targeted routing policy to move StratusCare traffic off eastus AZ1 into eastus2. Traffic is already shifting; early metrics show median latency improving (from ~1.2s -> ~210ms) for a subset of requests.
2) We kicked off a KV-prefix warm job in eastus2; cache seeding is ~50% complete. Soojin expects steady progress and full warm in ~12–15 minutes.
3) Marissa has put a remedial credit offer on the table (20% for the affected window) and the docs are attached.
4) We’d like to schedule a 30-minute bridge in 20 minutes to review the mitigation, confirm stability, and align on postmortem scope. Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.com/j/stratuscare-incident

We’ll monitor closely and I’ll keep you posted every 10 minutes until the situation is stable. Apologies for the interruption — we’re treating this as top priority.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
